deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page develops the cutting of an n-fold connected surface by cross-cuts (Querschnitte) into a simply connected one. It then applies this to integrals ∫(X dx + Y dy) with ∂X/∂y − ∂Y/∂x = 0. The next page is an outline (sections I–IV, p = 1, p = 2, p > 2) of the theory of Abelian functions. So this folio is a draft of the passage in 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), Vorbereitende Sätze, where Riemann moves from analysis situs to determining a function of a complex variable by boundary and discontinuity conditions via the Dirichlet principle.

PART 1 (heavily corrected prose). Approximately: 'We are therefore compelled here to a new presentation of this subject. In doing so we turn first exclusively to setting up a system of conditions by which, inside a given, arbitrarily bounded surface T covering the x,y-plane, a function of x+yi is completely determined.' No mathematics yet; this is the programme: existence and uniqueness of a holomorphic function w = u + iv on a (possibly multi-sheeted) region T, fixed by boundary and singularity data.

PART 2 (Dirichlet principle, fragmentary).
- 'Man denke sich …': the definition of the functional is not written out on this page (stopped after 'Man denke sich').
- From the parallel published texts (Dissertation §16; Abel'sche Functionen §3) it is Ω(ω) = ∬_T [(∂ω/∂x − ∂γ/∂y)² + (∂ω/∂y + ∂γ/∂x)²] dx dy, or simply ∬_T |∇ω|² dx dy. Here α is a given function carrying the prescribed boundary and singular behaviour. This identification is mine.
- Admissible class: 'Setzt man α − β für α, und für β alle stetigen an der Grenze verschwindenden Functionen'. That is, ω = α − β with β continuous on T and β = 0 on ∂T.
- Claim: 'so erhält das Integral immer einen endlichen, aber seiner Natur nach nie einen negativen Werth und hat nothwendig ein Minimum für eine Function u'.
- The minimum is meant in the sense that 'Ω für unendlich wenig von u verschiedene Functionen α − β > Ω(u) wird'. In modern terms: Ω(ω) ≥ 0, so inf Ω exists; Riemann asserts it is attained at some admissible u, at least as a local minimum.
- The last line begins the variational step: 'Setzt man hier [u + hβ, or α − β with] für β eine stetige Function …', and the page breaks off.

IMPLIED CONTINUATION (mine, following the published text). Put ω = u + hβ with β vanishing on ∂T. Then
- Ω(u + hβ) = Ω(u) + 2h ∬ (u_x β_x + u_y β_y) dT + h² ∬ |∇β|² dT.
- Minimality for all small h of both signs forces the linear term to vanish: ∬ ∇u·∇β = 0, i.e. −∬ β Δu = 0 for all such β.
- Hence Δu = 0, so u is harmonic and is the real part of a function of x+yi on simply connected pieces.
- The quadratic term gives uniqueness: Ω(u + β) = Ω(u) + Ω(β) > Ω(u) unless β ≡ 0.
- In the version with γ, the cross term ∬ (α_x γ_y − α_y γ_x) is a Jacobian. It reduces to a boundary integral, so minimising over α − β is equivalent to minimising the Dirichlet integral.

The faint symbols at the foot of the page appear to be show-through or doodles and carry no recoverable derivation.
errors: The inference 'Ω is never negative, therefore it necessarily has a minimum for some function u' is the famous gap in the Dirichlet principle. Nonnegativity guarantees only an infimum, not that it is attained in the class of continuous (C¹) functions vanishing on the boundary. Weierstrass criticised this in 1870 with his counterexample functional. It was repaired by Hilbert (1900/1904) and later by direct methods and Sobolev spaces.

The claim that the integral 'always' takes a finite value is unjustified for arbitrary continuous admissible functions. Hadamard (1906) gave continuous boundary data whose harmonic extension has infinite Dirichlet integral (Prym 1871 is a related example). Finiteness requires the admissible class to be restricted to functions of finite energy.

Local minimality is phrased only against 'infinitely little different' functions. The subsequent variational argument tacitly assumes enough regularity of u to integrate by parts. This regularity is not justified at this point.
The functional Ω is used but never defined on this page; the defining sentence breaks off after 'Man denke sich'. This is a draft issue, not a mathematical error.

results.what: Programme: determine a function of x+yi on an arbitrarily bounded (multi-sheeted) surface T covering the plane by boundary and discontinuity conditions.
results.modern_name: Boundary-value / existence problem for holomorphic (harmonic) functions on Riemann surfaces

results.what: Minimising the nonnegative energy Ω over α − β (β continuous, zero on the boundary) yields a minimiser u; varying β gives Δu = 0, and the minimiser is unique.
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle (variational solution of the Dirichlet problem / Euler–Lagrange equation for the Dirichlet integral)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1839), W. Thomson (1847), Dirichlet (lectures); named and used by Riemann (1851, 1857); rigorised by Hilbert (1900)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a well-known published passage: the Dirichlet-principle section of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper, paralleling Dissertation §16. It includes the very sentence ('nie einen negativen Werth … hat nothwendig ein Minimum') that Weierstrass later criticised. The draft wording (α − β for α) is of minor philological interest only.

checkable.asserts: For harmonic u and b vanishing on the boundary of the unit square, the first variation (cross term) of the Dirichlet integral is 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=Function('u')(x,y); from sympy.calculus.euler import euler_equations; euler_equations(diff(u,x)**2+diff(u,y)**2, u, [x,y])
checkable.asserts: The Euler–Lagrange equation of the Dirichlet integral is Δu = 0 (up to a factor of -2).
Riemann's integrand equals |∇α|²+|∇γ|² minus twice the Jacobian α_xγ_y − α_yγ_x (the Jacobian integrates to a boundary term); result 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); u=x**2-y**2; b=x*(1-x)*y*(1-y); E=lambda f: integrate(diff(f,x)**2+diff(f,y)**2,(x,0,1),(y,0,1)); simplify(E(u+b)-E(u)-E(b))
checkable.asserts: Ω(u+β) = Ω(u) + Ω(β) for harmonic u and β vanishing on the boundary, so u is the strict minimiser (uniqueness); result 0.
